page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64, equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, which yields a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, requiring external block storage solutions, and network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core metrics, such as the Geekbench single-core score and stress-ng single-core CPU performance, fall into the bottom 10% and 25% respectively, reflecting the lower clock speed of the older Intel Xeon architecture. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, achieve average tier results. Memory bandwidth tests show stable performance, with cached read speeds reaching 654.2 GB/sec and uncached read speeds at 75.3 GB/sec, though the Passmark memory score remains in the bottom 25%.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average multi-threaded performance, this instance is structured for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand high single-thread compute velocity. It is suitable for database operations, caching layers like Redis (which achieved 11.19 million SET operations per second in testing), and moderate web serving. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound applications where raw CPU speed is secondary to RAM capacity.
